title: Your launch email is going to spam

beats.say: You built the app, wrote the launch email, hit send, and it went straight to spam.

rows: We launched! Your early access is ready

beats.say: Since 2024, Gmail treats anyone sending five thousand emails a day as a bulk sender, with strict rules.

vis.sub: emails a day to Gmail = bulk sender

beats.say: First, three DNS records that prove the email is really from you. SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Most new apps have none.
Then one-click unsubscribe, and spam complaints under zero point three percent.
And Gmail has moved from delaying mail that breaks the rules, to rejecting it outright.
Even below five thousand, every sender needs SPF or DKIM. Set them up once, and every receipt and password reset lands too.
Here's the prompt. Screenshot it, and send it to Claude inside your project.
Follow Ship With Pip for one of these every day.

prompt: Check my app's email setup. Look up my domain's SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, confirm my email provider signs with DKIM on my domain, add List-Unsubscribe and one-click unsubscribe headers to marketing emails, and give me the exact DNS records to add.
caption: Gmail's sender rules: everyone needs SPF or DKIM; bulk senders (5,000+ emails/day to Gmail) need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, one-click unsubscribe, and spam complaints under 0.3%. Gmail went from deferring non-compliant mail to rejecting it. Fix three DNS records once and your launch emails, receipts and password resets actually arrive. The prompt is at the end.
sources: MailReach summary: 0.3% hard ceiling, 0.1% target; permanent 550 rejections from Nov 2025; 5.7.26 = unauthenticated
